methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective single-center case series/cohort of 50 patients with no comparator group, no sample-size or power calculation, and no multivariable adjustment for confounders such as age, histology, site, or latency when comparing surgical vs. systemic therapy. Selection bias is substantial: 10 patients were excluded for lack of follow-up without characterization, and the surgical cohort is systematically healthier (34% of non-surgical patients had unresectable disease and 18% had precluding comorbidities), making the headline comparison (5-year OS 57.5% vs 0%, p=0.000) essentially non-informative without adjustment. Multiple log-rank tests across subgroups (treatment, margins, histology) are reported without multiplicity correction, dose/fractionation data were acknowledged as incomplete, and causal attribution of tumors to prior radiotherapy relies solely on Cahan criteria without molecular confirmation. Statistical methods (Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Mann–Whitney) are elementary and appropriate in form but underpowered and insufficient for the causal/comparative claims made.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a retrospective single-center case series of 50 patients across a 21-year span with limited follow-up (mean 34.9 months) and substantial missing data on RT dose/fractionation and chemotherapy — this maps to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case series) rather than a true cohort 2b. Clinical relevance is moderate: head and neck RIMs are a genuinely important and under-studied late complication of curative RT, and the finding that surgical resection (particularly R0) confers survival advantage reinforces current practice recommendations and the need for lifelong surveillance. However, endpoints are limited to OS without PFS, functional, or quality-of-life measures, and the small, heterogeneous cohort does not establish practice-changing evidence beyond confirming existing recommendations in the literature.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies as this is an observational retrospective cohort/case series. Several key STROBE items are weakly addressed: there is no flow diagram of patient selection (only a narrative mention of 10 exclusions), inclusion/exclusion criteria are stated but contain typographical artifacts (criteria list with embedded periods instead of enumeration), outcomes are not clearly pre-specified vs. post-hoc (margin and histology subgroup analyses appear exploratory), confidence intervals are reported but no description of missing-data handling is given, and no protocol registration is mentioned. There is no data-availability statement, no code sharing, and no supplementary deposit of de-identified individual-level data — reproducibility is minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical contribution is incremental: another retrospective single-institution series of head and neck RIMs that largely confirms prior findings (e.g., Liu et al., Tay et al., Chung et al., Sale et al.) regarding surgical benefit, latency, and histologic distribution. The most interesting observation — that smokers with RIMs show a flattened SCC predominance and higher sarcoma frequency — is descriptive, not statistically significant, and based on very small subgroups. No new mechanism, assay, trial design, biomarker, or underserved population is introduced, and the manuscript appropriately positions itself as adding to a sparse literature rather than claiming field-defining novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is broadly readable and logically organized (Intro → Methods → Results with demographics/treatment/outcomes → Discussion → Conclusions), and the abstract pairs an accessible plain-language summary with a structured version. However, there are multiple typographical/grammatical lapses that should have been caught in copyediting: the criteria list in Methods uses periods instead of enumeration ('occurrence within the irradiated field.histological distinction...'), 'candided for palliative chemotherapy' (sic), 'Linical Characteristics' in reference 23, and inconsistent latency ranges (abstract says 3.4–36.25 years, discussion says 4–32 years, mean 20 vs 20.8 years). The R2 subgroup reporting (n=1 with '2-year OS 100%' then '70% at 2 years for R1+R2 combined') is confusing and the log-rank p=0.000 is poor convention (should be reported as p<0.001). Case descriptions and discussion are adequately clear but overlap with results.

key_strengths: Addresses a clinically meaningful and under-studied late complication of head and neck radiotherapy
Applies standard Cahan/Arlen/Murray diagnostic criteria consistently and acknowledges residual causal uncertainty
Reports Kaplan–Meier survival with 95% CIs across treatment and margin subgroups
Discussion situates findings against relevant prior single-institution series (Liu, Tay, Chung, Sale)
Honestly flags major limitations: missing dose/fractionation data, small n, retrospective monocentric design
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center case series of only 50 patients with no multivariable adjustment; the headline surgical survival benefit is almost certainly confounded by resectability/comorbidity selection
Multiple exploratory log-rank comparisons without multiplicity correction; p = 0.000 reported instead of p < 0.001
No power calculation, no missing-data handling described, 10 patients excluded for follow-up without characterization
Reporting falls well short of STROBE: no flow diagram, no data-availability statement, inclusion criteria list is typographically corrupted, latency range inconsistent between abstract and discussion
Novelty is incremental and largely confirmatory of existing single-institution series on head and neck RIMs
R2 subgroup (n=1) survival interpretation and smokers-histology subgroup inferences are overreaching given the sample
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently conducted but highly incremental retrospective single-center case series with modest sample size, no comparator cohort, no multivariable analysis, and weak STROBE adherence. Content fits a Tier 4 narrow-scope oncology outlet after addressing typographical errors, statistical reporting conventions, a STROBE flow diagram, and clearer framing of the surgery-vs-systemic comparison as hypothesis-generating.
